Travel planning app Tripsy updated this week with support for iOS 27's extra-large widgets, a new Smart Import tool, AI-powered features, and other improvements. Details below.

Tripsy update adds AI-powered features

During Apple's "Surprise and Shine" event, Apple briefly mentioned the independently developed travel planning app Tripsy while showing off some of iOS 27's new Siri AI capabilities. Apple published an iOS 27 press release earlier this week highlighting that Siri will soon be able to add restaurant recommendations directly to Tripsy.

The app, which was also a finalist for the 2024 App Store Awards, updated to version 3.10 earlier this week with new features including AI-powered tools and support for iOS 27 features.

These include the new Smart Import feature, which can convert links, documents (including PDFs), saved emails, screenshots, accessible webpages of Instagram and TikTok posts, and pasted text into locations and bookings within the app.

Smart Import also supports importing lists and guides from Google Maps and Apple Maps, and lets users pick which suggested items they actually want to add to their trip.

Similarly, this update also introduces Smart Insights, a feature that uses Apple's Foundation Models to analyse attached documents and emails on-device, and displays useful trip details such as baggage allowances, breakfast, parking, cancellation policies and fees.

Other improvements in Tripsy 3.10 include:

  • Support for iOS 27 extra-large iPhone widgets, offering a more complete view of your itinerary.
  • Improved travel stats updates, map stability, and Mac import layout.
  • Improved location suggestions, including options to access all hotels in a trip, and the option to turn off departure suggestions for airports you no longer need.

Tripsy notes that Smart Import and Smart Insights are Pro subscription features, priced at $39 per year or $199 for lifetime access.
